claims.quote: Low-grade fever; Enlarged, tender lymph nodes that develop 1–3 weeks after exposure to a cat; A papule or pustule at the site of the scratch

claims.text: Table: lymph nodes enlarge 1 to 3 weeks after exposure

claims.text: Prevention bullets: avoid scratches/bites/licks esp. kittens and strays; wash hands; clean scratch with soap and water; flea prevention, never permethrin on cats; keep cats indoors
claims.quote: Avoid cat scratches, bites, and licks, especially from kittens or stray cats. ... Wash hands promptly after handling cats. Clean scratch wounds with soap and water.

claims.text: Prevention bullets (continued): flea prevention, no permethrin, indoors
claims.quote: Talk to your veterinarian about flea prevention products for your cat. Never use products that contain permethrin on cats. Keep cats indoors and away from stray cats.

claims.text: Fever, pustule at the scratch site, and eye involvement are reasons to see a clinician (in-person list, Nov 18)
claims.quote: See a healthcare provider if you or your child develops a fever; enlarged, tender lymph nodes that develop 1–3 weeks after being scratched; or a pustule at the scratch site. ... Rarely, infections of the eye, liver, spleen, brain, bones, or heart valves can occur.

claims.text: Key fact: CSD usually follows a scratch from a domestic or feral cat, especially a kitten
claims.quote: People usually get CSD after being scratched by domestic or feral cats, especially kittens.

claims.text: Key fact / FAQ: Bartonella found in blood of up to 1 in 3 healthy cats, particularly kittens
claims.quote: Some studies have found the Bartonella bacteria in the blood of up to 1 in 3 healthy cats, particularly kittens.

claims.text: Most cat scratches do not result in CSD
claims.quote: Most cat scratches do not result in CSD.

claims.text: More common in children under 15, in the Southeast, mostly fall and winter; stray cats more likely infected
claims.quote: CSD is more common among children under the age of 15 ... more common in the Southeast ... most cases of CSD occur in the fall and winter. ... Stray cats are more likely than pet cats to be infected

claims.text: Most infected cats show no illness
claims.quote: While some cats become ill, most simply have the bacteria in their blood without getting sick.

claims.text: Immunocompromised at higher risk of severe CSD; antibiotics recommended for all immunocompromised
claims.quote: people with weakened immune systems are at higher risk for severe CSD ... is recommended for all patients who are immunocompromised (have a weakened immune system).

claims.text: Examples of weakened immune system: advanced HIV, cancer treatment
claims.quote: occur primarily in people with weakened immune systems, such as those with advanced HIV infection. ... living with HIV, are being treated for cancer, or have another condition that might suppress your immune system.

claims.quote: People who have weakened immune systems should avoid owning cats less than one-year-old. ... Keep your cat indoors. You do not need to test or treat your cat for B. henselae if it is healthy.

claims.text: Endocarditis with blood cultures often negative

claims.text: Declawing not recommended to prevent CSD
claims.quote: Declawing cats is not recommended to prevent CSD.

claims.text: FAQ: bites or licks of open wounds can spread it; flea-bite spread not proven

claims.text: Exposure risks: kittens, stray or feral cats, fleas
claims.quote: Bartonella henselae bacteria, which can be carried by fleas. ... scratched by domestic or feral cats, particularly kittens. Stray cats are more likely than pet cats to be infected
